title: Godot 4 (GDScript) → three.js (TypeScript, browser)
conventions: three.js is a renderer, not a game engine: physics, input mapping, scene files, audio buses and UI are yours to choose. A common stack: three + Rapier (@dimforge/rapier3d-compat) for physics, plain DOM/CSS for UI, Vite for building.

Axes match Godot (right-handed, Y up, cameras look down -Z, meters): positions and quaternions carry over unchanged. Godot's default Euler order is YXZ; set object.rotation.order = 'YXZ' when copying Euler angles.

Godot scenes: export meshes and materials as glTF 2.0 (Scene → Export As → glTF 2.0) and load them with GLTFLoader; recreate the node logic in TypeScript classes that own an Object3D. ReversePort can write a TypeScript scene-builder module from a .tscn (port_scene).
Each GDScript becomes a TypeScript class with update(dt) and fixedUpdate(dt) methods; a small game loop calls them from renderer.setAnimationLoop.
Dispose geometries, materials and textures when removing objects (the browser does not free GPU memory for you).
